newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London closed mostly higher in quiet trade. December closed unchanged at $325.00 while March shed $0.90 to close at $322.20.

In New York raw sugar futures settled sharply firmer on trade and speculative buying. A dearth of selling interest contributed to firmer prices. March added 22 points to close at 10.89 cents/lb while May closed 16 points higher at 10.82 cents/lb. Most of today's advance was technical, as fundamentals do not point to a noticeable rise in sugar prices.

MALAYSIA - Sugar imports in May 1996 amounted to 96,900 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on last year's 95,030 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996 (January/May) up to 416,167 tonnes against 356,292 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 hit the record high of 1.03 million tonnes compared to 959,518 tonnes in 1994.
The sole countries of origin in January/May 1996 were Thailand with 294,800 tonnes raws against 159,796 tonnes and Australia with 121,367 tonnes compared to 182,230 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1996 reached 10,024 tonnes, up from 7,166 tonnes exported in May 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/May 1996 up to 45,244 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 41,116 tonnes. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 123,561 tonnes against 159,525 tonnes in 1994.
Major countries of destination in January/May 1996 were Singapore with 26,160 tonnes whites and Indonesia with 12,069 tonnes.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in August 1996 amounted to 19,940 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on last year's 17,911 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first eight months of 1996 (January/August) up to 122,572 tonnes compared to 110,641 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 amounted to 173,712 tonnes, down from 192,368 tonnes imported in calendar year 1994.
Major countries of origin in January/August 1996 were Denmark with 72,621 tonnes whites against 73,050 tonnes and the United Kingdom with 27,992 tonnes compared to 24,137 tonnes.
GERMANY - The fifth German beet test of September 27, 1996 shows a satisfactory increase in sugar content while growth in root weight remained below average.

Sugar content on September 27 amounted to 17.8 per cent, up on last year's 16.4 per cent and above the five-year average (1991/95) of 16.9 per cent. Root weight per ha reached 62.22 tonnes, slightly up on the previous year's 61.62 tonnes and above the five-year average of 60.86 tonnes.
This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 11.10 tonnes per ha, white value, up more than 10 per cent on the previous year's 10.08 tonnes and also significantly above the average of 10.27 tonnes.
The data suggest that Germany is heading for a very satisfactory crop in 1996 and the latest forecasts are for an overall white sugar output of 3.895 million tonnes.
TURKEY - The latest beet test results of August 30 suggest that the sugar crop has again fallen behind the results of 1995 despite a slightly higher sugar content.

Root weight per ha amounted to 41.64 tonnes, down from last year's 42.67 tonnes while sugar content reached 14.7 per cent against 14.6 per cent in 1995. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 6.13 tonnes, white value, per ha, compared to 6.23 tonnes in 1995.

However, due to a signficantly higher area sown to beet, the country is heading for a substantially bigger crop in 1996 and the Turkish sugar industry estimates that an overall total of 1.85 million tonnes, white value, can be achieved.
